one_liner: Time tracking and invoicing platform that helps teams log billable hours, manage projects, and bill clients.

auth.notes: Personal Access Token (bearer_token) or OAuth2. Personal tokens are static tokens sent as Bearer in Authorization header. OAuth2 supports server-side (Authorization Code) and client-side (Implicit Grant) flows.

evidence.snippet: The V2 API requires an access token to authenticate requests. There are two options available to you: A Personal Access Token which is tied directly to you and is the quickest way to start playing around with the API. Implementing a full OAuth2 Authentication flow which allows other people to use your Harvest integrations.
Once generated, a Personal Access Token can be used to access the API by either providing the token in the Authorization header or including it in the query string.

access.notes: Developers can sign up for a 30-day free trial without credit card and create a Personal Access Token immediately. After 30 days, trial account is deactivated. A Free plan tier exists but whether API access is available post-trial on free plan is not documented in provided pages.

evidence.snippet: Get started on any plan with a free trial. No credit card required.
The API can be accessed by creating a Personal Access Token from the Developers section of Harvest ID.
If you haven't upgraded at the end of 30 days, your trial account will be automatically deactivated.

buildability.rationale: Composio toolkit already built with 57 tools and Composio-managed OAuth available today.

overview_evidence.snippet: Harvest helps professional teams track time, bill clients, optimize team time, and measure performance with confidence.
Harvest is a time-tracking and invoicing tool designed for teams and freelancers, helping them log billable hours, manage projects, and streamline payments

unknown_reasons.access: Pages do not explicitly document whether API access is included on free plan tier after 30-day trial period ends.
unknown_reasons.mcp: No vendor-published MCP server identified in provided pages; no community MCP server repositories documented in provided pages.
